pr.title: fix(gemm): order the stage release, output stores and loader exit of the warp split-K BF16 GEMM
pr.body:
[by Claude Code]

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Fixes three synchronization orderings that the PTX memory model does not guarantee in `CpAsyncWarpSplitKKernel` (`flashinfer/gemm/kernels/dense_bf16_gemm_warp_splitk.py`, the warp split-K runner of `mm_bf16(backend="cute-dsl")`); details in #8080. Tiles, K slices, MMA order, reduction order and rounding are unchanged, so outputs are bitwise identical to main.

1. **Output stores under PDL.** Only the activation-loader warps executed `griddepcontrol.wait`; the warp that stores the output was ordered after the prerequisite grids only through the loaders' asynchronous `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive`. With `use_pdl`, the storing warp now executes `griddepcontrol.wait` before its stores. The prerequisite grids have already completed by then (the stores depend on activation tiles that the loaders read after their own wait), so it never waits on a running grid.
2. **Stage reuse.** One elected lane per compute warp arrived on a stage's empty barrier (count 4), but `mbarrier.try_wait` orders only the arriving threads' prior accesses, so the other lanes' `ldmatrix` reads were not ordered before the loaders' next `cp.async` into the stage. Every compute lane now arrives (count 4 x 32).
3. **Loader exit.** Loader threads exited with `cp.async` copies in flight, which the PTX ISA does not define. Each loader path now ends with `cp.async.wait_all` (on the activation-loader path after `launch_dependents`, so the dependent launch is not delayed).

New test `tests/gemm/test_mm_bf16_warp_splitk_sync.py` compiles the kernel on the host for sm_100a and sm_103a (no GPU needed) and checks the three orderings in the generated PTX, as `tests/moe/test_b12x_w4a16_grid_barrier.py` does for its barrier. These orderings change no result, so a replay test cannot tell the two kernels apart.

The fix was validated on Vera Rubin NVL72 (SM107) on v0.7.2 (the same three hunks: #6833 changed only `autotune_tactics` in this file) and re-validated on B300 (SM103) on main e7ee9232e.

### Performance (kernel microbenchmark)

In situ: a CUDA graph of [predecessor -> GEMM -> successor] layers with distinct weights in every layer (about 512 MiB of weights per graph; the cap of 78 layers gives 146 MiB at 160 x 6144 and 468 MiB at 6144 x 512), `pdl=True`, FlashInfer RMSNorm or SiLU-and-mul before and after the GEMM (a BMM before 6144 x 4096). Each run pairs this PR's kernel against main's kernel, loaded as separate modules, with a second copy of main's kernel as an A/A control: 21 repeats x 10 replays per arm, arm order rotated every repeat. Per call = (PR - main) / (the GEMM's marginal in-graph time).

**B300, the default tactic** (what `mm_bf16(backend="cute-dsl")` runs without autotuning), 16 decode shapes, 4-5 runs per shape:

| N x K | M | tactic (output, token, k tile, stages, B loaders) | main (us per layer) | PR - main (us) | per call |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6144 x 4096 | 1 / 4 / 5 | (16, 8, 256, 9, 2) | 14.7 / 15.3 / 15.3 | -0.12 to -0.01 | -1.2% to -0.1% |
| 6144 x 4096 | 20 | (16, 32, 256, 4, 2) | 19.8 | -0.13 to -0.09 | -0.9% to -0.6% |
| 2624 x 6144 | 1 / 4 / 5 | (32, 8, 256, 11, 2) | 9.9 / 10.6 / 10.6 | -0.19 to +0.01 | -3.0% to +0.2% |
| 2624 x 6144 | 20 | (32, 32, 256, 6, 2) | 13.0 | +0.00 to +0.06 | +0.0% to +0.7% |
| 6144 x 512 | 1 / 4 / 5 | (16, 8, 128, 4, 1) | 6.1 / 6.6 / 6.6 | +0.01 to +0.03 | +0.2% to +0.9% |
| 160 x 6144 | 5 | (16, 8, 256, 16, 2) | 7.1 | -0.20 | -5.1% to -4.9% |
| 1024 x 6144 | 1 / 4 / 5 | (16, 8, 256, 16, 2) | 6.9 / 7.7 / 7.8 | -0.28 to -0.23 | -6.2% to -5.1% |
| **1024 x 6144** | **20** | **(16, 16, 256, 13, 2)** | 8.5 | **+0.40 to +0.43** | **+7.9% to +8.4%** |

**B300 at SM107's default tactics** (`default_tactic` depends on the SM count; these are the tactics it picks on Vera Rubin NVL72 for the same shapes. On B300 all of them except (32, 8, 128, 4, 1) fall outside the autotune space, so they were passed explicitly), 5 runs: M <= 5 with token tile 8 is 2.7% to 4.8% faster per call at 6144 x 4096 and 2624 x 6144; slower in every run are 2624 x 6144 M=20 at (16, 32, 256, 9, 2) (+3.8% to +4.6%), 6144 x 4096 M=20 at (32, 32, 256, 6, 2) (+2.2% to +2.5%) and 6144 x 512 at (32, 8, 128, 4, 1) (+1.9% to +3.1%).

**Vera Rubin NVL72 (SM107)**, v0.7.2 with the same three hunks, the 16 shapes at SM107's default tactics, 2 runs: -4.5% to +0.9% per call in the first run and -4.4% to +1.4% in the second; 15 of 16 shapes stay at or below +0.9% in both, and 1024 x 6144 M=20 measured +0.1% and +1.4%.

Attribution (B300, single-fix variants of the kernel, same bench, one run): the speedups at token tile 8 come mostly from `cp.async.wait_all` (also seen on SM107; the mechanism is not established). Where the fix costs most, the per-lane empty-barrier arrive is most of it: +0.36 us of the +0.41 us at 1024 x 6144 M=20 (16, 16, 256, 13, 2), and +0.56 us of +0.61 us at 2624 x 6144 M=20 (16, 32, 256, 9, 2). In the sm_103a SASS that arrive is a `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.A1T0` executed by every lane; on SM107 it lowered to a single warp-uniform `USYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.ACT0`. At 6144 x 4096 M=20 (32, 32, 256, 6, 2) the cost comes mostly from items 1 and 3 instead. See the Reviewer Notes for a cheaper form of item 2.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Fixes #8080

Related: #7591 (open) makes the compute warps wait before the bias read when the kernel has a bias. It edits nearby lines of the same file; the two changes merge without conflict. With both, a kernel with a bias waits twice in the storing warp, and the second wait returns without waiting on any grid.

+"""Synchronization of the warp split-K BF16 GEMM
+(flashinfer/gemm/kernels/dense_bf16_gemm_warp_splitk.py, a runner of
+``mm_bf16(backend="cute-dsl")``), checked in its generated PTX.
+
+These are memory-model orderings: the kernel returns the same, correct results
+with or without them, so a replay or stress test cannot tell them apart. The
+test compiles the kernel on the host (no GPU needed) and inspects the PTX.
+"""
+
+import re
+
+import pytest
+
+# K = 6144 is 24 tiles of 256 over a 16-stage ring, so stages are reused.
+_N, _K = 1024, 6144
+# (output_tile, token_tile, k_tile, stages, b_loader_warps)
+_TACTIC = (16, 8, 256, 16, 2)
+_LOADER_THREADS = (2 + _TACTIC[4]) * 32
+_COMPUTE_THREADS = 4 * 32
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=["sm_100a", "sm_103a"])
+def ptx(request, tmp_path_factory) -> str:
+    from flashinfer.cute_dsl.availability import is_cute_dsl_experimental_available
+
+    if not is_cute_dsl_experimental_available():
+        pytest.skip("nvidia-cutlass-dsl with cutlass.experimental is not available.")
+    import cutlass
+    from cutlass import cute
+    from cutlass.cute import experimental as cute_ext
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream, make_fake_tensor
+
+    from flashinfer.gemm.kernels.dense_bf16_gemm_warp_splitk import (
+        CpAsyncWarpSplitKKernel,
+        WarpSplitKTactic,
+    )
+
+    # The operands run_warp_splitk_dense passes: row-major, with a dynamic
+    # 32-bit M (the PTX then matches the runtime JIT build).
+    bf16 = cutlass.BFloat16
+    weight = make_fake_tensor(bf16, (_N, _K), (_K, 1), assumed_align=32)
+    activation = make_fake_tensor(
+        bf16, (cute.sym_int32(), _K), (_K, 1), assumed_align=32
+    )
+    bias = make_fake_tensor(bf16, (_N,), (1,), assumed_align=32)
+    output = make_fake_tensor(bf16, (cute.sym_int32(), _N), (_N, 1), assumed_align=32)
+    dump_dir = tmp_path_factory.mktemp(request.param)
+    compiled = cute_ext.compile(
+        CpAsyncWarpSplitKKernel(WarpSplitKTactic(*_TACTIC), True, False),
+        weight,
+        activation,
+        bias,
+        output,
+        make_fake_stream(),
+        options=f"--gpu-arch {request.param} --keep-ptx --dump-dir {dump_dir}",
+    )
+    assert compiled.__ptx__ is not None
+    return compiled.__ptx__
+
+
+def test_output_stores_wait_for_prerequisite_grids(ptx):
+    # Under PDL only the activation loaders execute griddepcontrol.wait; the
+    # warp that stores the output must wait too (after the split-K reduction
+    # barrier, before its first store) for its stores to be ordered after the
+    # prerequisite grids, whose memory `out` may reuse.
+    first_store = ptx.index("st.global")
+    barriers = [m.end() for m in re.finditer(r"\bbar(?:rier)?\.sync\b", ptx)]
+    reduction = max(i for i in barriers if i < first_store)
+    assert "griddepcontrol.wait" in ptx[reduction:first_store]
+
+
+def test_every_compute_lane_releases_the_stage(ptx):
+    # Every compute lane reads a stage with ldmatrix before the loaders may
+    # overwrite it. mbarrier.try_wait orders only the arriving threads' prior
+    # accesses, so every lane arrives on the empty barrier (count 128) rather
+    # than one elected lane per warp (count 4).
+    counts, movs = [], {}
+    for line in ptx.splitlines():
+        mov = re.search(r"mov\.[bsu]32\s+(%r\d+),\s*(\d+);", line)
+        if mov:
+            movs[mov.group(1)] = int(mov.group(2))
+        init = re.search(r"mbarrier\.init\.shared\.b64\s+\[.+\],\s*(%r\d+|\d+);", line)
+        if init:
+            count = init.group(1)
+            counts.append(int(count) if count.isdigit() else movs[count])
+    # Full barrier (every loader thread), then empty barrier (every compute lane).
+    assert counts == [_LOADER_THREADS, _COMPUTE_THREADS]
+    assert "elect.sync" not in ptx
+
+
+def test_loaders_drain_cp_async_before_exit(ptx):
+    # The weight and activation loader threads exit right after their last
+    # cp.async.mbarrier.arrive; the PTX ISA does not define a thread exiting
+    # with cp.async copies in flight, so each loader path drains them first.
+    assert ptx.count("cp.async.wait_all") >= 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    pytest.main([__file__])
